title: BizFlood Cancellation at the Insured's Request — Earned Premium and Return
content:
**Rule.** A cancellation of a BizFlood Commercial Flood Policies (Surplus Lines) policy is processed only on a cancellation request signed by an authorized signer of the insured and on file for the policy. It takes effect on the date the signed request is received or a later date named in it. The earned premium is the larger of the pro rata share of the term premium to the cancellation date and the tier's minimum earned premium percentage of the term premium; the policy fee and inspection fees are earned when the tier does not return fees on cancellation; tax and stamping fee are returned on the returned premium at the recorded rates when the tier returns taxes with returned premium. Nothing is returned when a claim with a date of loss in the term has a net payment above zero.

## Authority and object

- The request must be a cancellation request signed by an authorized signer of the insured, and it must be on file for this policy in Tidemark's records. What the records hold on file is the authority; a request that is described but not on file for the policy does not meet the condition.
- The request on file belongs to the policy being cancelled; a request on file for another policy does not serve.
- A policy cancelled this way may be active or still pending effective.

## Effective date

| The signed request | Cancellation takes effect |
|---|---|
| Names no date later than the date it is received | On the date the signed request is received |
| Names a date later than its receipt | On that later date |

## Claims in the term

Nothing is returned when, within the current policy term — from the term start, counted in, to the term end, counted out, judged by each claim's date of loss — at least one claim has a net payment above zero, net payment being the claim payments issued less the payments voided.

| A claim on the policy | Effect on the return |
|---|---|
| Date of loss in the current term; payments issued exceed payments voided | Nothing is returned |
| Date of loss in the current term; every payment issued was voided, net payment zero | It does not stop the return |
| Date of loss in the current term; no payment issued | It does not stop the return |
| Date of loss before the current term started | It does not stop the return |

## Worked cases (hypothetical figures)

Assume a 365-day term, a term premium of 3,650.00, a minimum earned premium percentage of 25 percent, fees not returned, taxes returned with premium, and recorded rates of 4 percent surplus lines tax and 0.4 percent stamping fee; no claim in the term has a net payment above zero.

| | Cancellation after 73 days of the term | Cancellation after 292 days of the term |
|---|---|---|
| Pro rata share to the cancellation date | 3,650.00 multiplied by 73, divided by 365: 730.00 | 3,650.00 multiplied by 292, divided by 365: 2,920.00 |
| 25 percent of the term premium | 912.50 | 912.50 |
| Earned premium (the larger) | 912.50 | 2,920.00 |
| Returned premium (term premium less earned premium) | 2,737.50 | 730.00 |
| Tax returned on the returned premium | 109.50 | 29.20 |
| Stamping fee returned on the returned premium | 10.95 | 2.92 |
| Policy fee and inspection fees | Earned, not returned | Earned, not returned |

If, in either case, a claim with a date of loss in the term had a net payment above zero, nothing would be returned.
